findings.text: Deferred removal carrier pairs a work queue item with a pointer to the affected cpuset so a later worker can locate its target.
Rate decay coefficient equals 933, described as giving about ten seconds half life.
Per-update elapsed tick cap equals 99, beyond which further decay steps are treated as useless.
Pending event count saturation limit equals 1000000, preventing overflow.
Faux fixed point scale for the rate estimator equals 1000.

Rate meter starts with zeroed count, value and time. Update uses whole seconds since last stamp, returns early when none elapsed, otherwise caps elapsed, repeatedly attenuates stored value by coefficient over scale, restamps time, then folds pending count weighted by complement of coefficient and clears count. Mark adds one scaled unit saturating at maximum, get returns decayed value.
Meter count, value and timestamp are guarded by its own spinlock initialized at setup. Mark and get hold it across update plus access; update itself expects the caller to already hold it.
A widely visible flag controls memory pressure tracking. The bump helper records one event against the calling task current cpuset meter while holding an RCU read guard.

Relax level update on SMP rejects values below minus one or above scheduler maximum plus one, applies only on change, and rebuilds scheduler domains when allowed CPUs are non-empty and load balancing is enabled. The 64-bit control writer takes the full lock, requires online state, serves only the relax file with a one-time deprecation notice, and rejects other files. The reader returns the stored level and faults on unknown file types.

Full acquisition order is top mutex, then CPUs read guard, then cpuset mutex; release reverses that order. The CPUs-held assertion is silent before running state and otherwise asserts the hotplug guard is held.

Services provided outside these fragments include pressure bump, scheduler domain rebuild, full lock pair, callback lock pair, task CPU and node mask refreshers, mm reference and executable-file helpers, and legacy spread, hotplug, validation and domain generation operations.

Active domain rebuild requires CPU and cpuset locks held, clears the forced-rebuild request, builds domain masks and attributes, verifies every domain lies within active CPUs with a one-time warning, freeing outputs and aborting on violation, otherwise hands them to the scheduler partition installer. The alternate build is an empty no-operation.

Version selection reports v2 when legacy support is disabled or the subsystem is on the default hierarchy. The v2 generator delegates to legacy when not v2, fast-paths a single full domain when no subpartition CPUs exist, otherwise collects valid partition roots with non-empty effective CPUs under RCU while pruning subtrees lacking validity and exclusive CPUs, warns on overlaps, allocates domains with optionally default-initialized attributes, masks the top domain by boot housekeeping CPUs and others by their effective CPUs, and reports one domain with a null pointer on allocation failure for caller fallback.

Legacy generator requires the cpuset lock. It fast-paths one domain when the top set is load balancing, intersected with housekeeping domain CPUs and with tree-derived attributes. Otherwise it gathers load-balanced sets with non-empty effective CPUs while skipping empty or non-balancing subtrees, merges overlapping entries with union-find over per-set nodes, counts distinct sets, builds one mask per set by combining member effective sets and intersecting housekeeping CPUs while folding attributes, checks slot accounting, and likewise falls back to one null domain on allocation failure.
Attribute update keeps the maximum relax level seen. Tree update walks descendants under RCU, prunes whole subtrees with empty allowed CPUs, and folds only load-balanced members.
Partition validity holds exactly when the stored root state is positive.

Neutral inline variants exist for spread updates, hotplug updates, change validation, exclusivity test, initialization, online notification and domain generation, doing nothing or returning zero or false. The real per-task spread updater is inert on the default hierarchy and otherwise sets or clears page spreading per the cpuset flag; the bulk variant walks every task in the set applying it.

Empty-set handling climbs to the nearest ancestor having both CPUs and memory, then transfers tasks with error logging. Hotplug emptying a populated set defers that transfer: take an online reference, allocate a carrier, queue work, then the worker performs the transfer, drops the reference and frees the carrier, with a warning and reference drop on allocation failure.

Legacy hotplug update copies new CPU and memory masks into both allowed and effective sets under the callback guard, refreshes task CPU masks only when CPUs changed and allowed CPUs remain, refreshes node masks only when memory changed and allowed memory remains, and treats emptiness as either mask being empty.
Callback protection is an interrupt-disabling spin guard with paired lock and unlock helpers.

Task CPU mask refresh iterates tasks in the set. For the top set it skips kernel and no-affinity tasks and uses task-possible CPUs minus subpartition CPUs; for other sets it intersects task-possible CPUs with the set effective CPUs, then applies the result as affinity.

Node mask refresh publishes a being-rebound marker to catch forks, computes a guaranteed-online mask, updates every task nodemask, and for thread leaders only acquires an mm reference, rebinds policy to effective memory, and migrates pages when enabled, otherwise dropping the reference. It finally records the new mask as old and clears the marker. Per-task update holds the task lock with interrupts disabled across a sequence-guarded change that unions then replaces allowed nodes and rebinds task policy.

Online-memory guarantee climbs parents until effective memory intersects online nodes. The mm migrator drops its reference immediately when source equals destination, otherwise allocates a work item carrying mm and masks and queues it on the dedicated workqueue, dropping the reference if allocation fails.

Mm reference release may sleep and runs full teardown only when the last user departs. Teardown clears uprobe state, asynchronous IO, shared-memory and huge-page daemon state before unmapping, unmaps, releases the huge zero folio, clears the executable file, removes the object from the global list under its lock when linked, drops the binary-format module when present, then releases reverse-mapping, futex hash and address-space references.

Executable-file replacement denies write access on the new file and fails on denial, takes a reference, publishes the pointer, then re-allows write and drops the old file when present. Task mm acquisition returns null for kernel threads, otherwise locks the task, takes a reference when an mm is present, unlocks and returns it.

Subset test requires CPU subset, memory subset, and nondecreasing CPU and memory exclusivity. Change validation expects an RCU read guard, rejects when any child would not be a subset of the trial, rejects when the trial would not be a subset of the parent on legacy hierarchy, rejects when a populated set would newly empty CPUs or memory, and otherwise succeeds.

Supplying offline CPUs to the scheduler partition installer can panic, so rebuild validates subset membership and aborts with a warning. Domain and pointer-array allocation failures fall back to a single default domain with a null pointer. Concurrent memory rebind is serialized by the global mutex protecting the shared mask and rebind marker, and migration paths always drop mm references.
